name: Front Brake Pads
primaryScope: PRIMARY found for: (a) OE parts catalog (RealOEM, type code PH73 USA, selection 09/2009, E90N 328i): front pad kit 34116790759 (from 09/2009), driver-front wear sensor 34356789440 (up to 03/2010), 312x24 front rotor 34118848417 (up to 04/2011), carrier screw, guiding bolt, caps, retaining spring, anti-squeal paste, plus the catalog statements that pads, sensor and paste are mandatory together and that the retaining spring is to be replaced on cars over 48 months old; (b) BMW owner's manual text for a 2011 E90 328i (third-party text mirror; the 2010 US sedan manual itself only came back as an unreadable binary): brakes need an initial break-in of approx. 300 miles/500 km, jacking points are 'at the positions shown in the illustration' (positions are not described in the text), and the service display tracks front brake pads, rear brake pads and brake fluid. NO BMW primary found for any torque, for the rotor discard thickness, for the wheel-bolt torque (not in the retrievable owner's manual text) or for the wear-sensor/CBS reset procedure.
summary: Third pass resolved most gaps using the RealOEM catalog for this car (PH73 USA, 09/2009) and BMW owner's manual text (2011 E90 328i mirror). Parts: pad kit 34116790759, driver-front sensor 34356789440 with clip 34356779356, 312x24 rotor 34118848417, retaining springs 34116776526, paste 83192158851 and the guiding bolts 34111157041; the catalog says sensor and paste are mandatory with the pads and the spring is to be replaced on cars over 48 months. Rotor discard thickness is 22.4 mm per four rotor-maker sources (VERIFIED_SECONDARY). Jacking is limited to the four side pads (center-point forum conflict left out). BMW's break-in is 500 km (300 miles), replacing Autodoc's shorter figure. Guide-pin torque 30 Nm, carrier-bolt 110 Nm, rotor screw 16 Nm and wheel-bolt 120 Nm remain secondary (3+ independent hosts, no BMW document, primary:false). Still open: carrier-bolt head type (Torx per catalog vs 18 mm hex per guides), wheel-liner fastener torque, guide-pin hex 6 vs 7 mm, and a BMW torque document.
variantDependencies: VIN WBAPH7C58AA175760 decodes at NHTSA vPIC (check digit valid) to: BMW 328i, 2010, Sedan, 3.0 L, 230 hp, Munich, TPMS Direct. [https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeVinValues/WBAPH7C58AA175760?format=json&modelyear=2010]

Drive and build date (VIN-DECODE.md, bimmer.work and RealOEM; probable, not proven): rear-wheel drive (PH73 type code), start of production 09/2009. Consequences used here: front sensor 34356789440 (valid to 03/2010) rather than the xDrive sensors, and pad kit 34116790759 (from 09/2009). If a parts counter supplies 34356792560 instead, Bimmerworld lists it as the successor of 34356789440.

Brake package: RealOEM's front brake diagrams for this car apply to cars without the usable-load-increase / reinforced-brakes options (S100A=No, S102A=No) and without Performance Parts; the VIN decode shows no sport/M brake option. Front rotor 312x24 is then the catalog size. Identify it yourself: the rotor diameter and MIN TH are stamped on the rotor, and the old pads must match the new kit; if they do not, stop and get the correct kit by VIN.
Engine N52B30 vs N51B30 (RealOEM E90N / bimmer.work N52K vs N52N labels differ): no source shows the pad job differing.
Transmission: no source shows any effect on this job.

Front caliper guide-pin head: sources agree on a hex socket head (7 mm FCP/Autodoc, 6 mm in one Pelican staff reply). BMW-data table also lists a hexagon-head guide screw at 35 Nm for some cars; RealOEM lists a single guiding-bolt number (34111157041) for this car. Check the head before applying a torque.
Carrier bolt head: RealOEM/Turner call it a Torx screw, Febi and the how-to guides a hex bolt (18 mm). Look at the head before choosing a socket.

Wheel: VIN decode lists style 285 (RealOEM: 8Jx17 ET34, wheel bolt M12x1.5 36136781150). Tire/run-flat status is not coded; it does not change the brake procedure except that no spare wheel is carried (owner's manual: run-flat tires, no spare).

tools.item: Floor jack, rated jack stands (2 minimum, 4 if lifting the whole car), wheel chocks
17 mm wheel-bolt socket (1/2 in drive), breaker bar
7 mm hex (Allen) socket for the two front caliper guide pins (a 6 mm bit fit poorly on some cars)
tools.conflicts: One Pelican staff reply says a 6 mm bit worked on its car while a reader found 6 mm too large; FCP and Autodoc both say 7 mm. Use 7 mm and test fit.

tools.item: 18 mm socket (deep, 3/8 or 1/2 in drive) for the two caliper carrier bolts, only if the carrier or rotor comes off
tools.conflicts: RealOEM names the carrier bolt 34106864424 'Torx screw with washer' (M12x1.5x43) and Turner calls it a Torx bolt (E-Torx size not stated), while Febi sells the same OE number as a 'caliper hex bolt' and four how-to sources (FCP, Autodoc, DriveDIY, Pelican) call for an 18 mm hex socket. Look at the bolt heads before choosing a socket: a hexagon head takes the 18 mm socket; a star-shaped (external Torx) head needs a matching external-Torx socket whose size was not found. Do not force an 18 mm socket onto a star head.

tools.item: 6 mm hex bit for the rotor retaining screw, only if replacing rotors
Torque wrench covering 16 to 120 Nm (about 12 to 90 lb-ft); ideally a small one for 30 Nm and a large one for 110/120 Nm
Piston wind-back tool, large C-clamp or caliper spreader (front piston is pushed straight in, no twisting needed per the sources)
Flat-blade screwdriver and pliers or needle-nose pliers (anti-rattle spring, sensor, caps)
8 mm and 10 mm nut drivers or sockets and a Phillips screwdriver, only if the wheel-liner must be loosened to reach the sensor connector
Wire brush, brake cleaner, silicone-based caliper grease for guide pins, anti-squeal paste for pad-to-carrier contact points
Micrometer or vernier caliper to measure rotor thickness against the stamped minimum
Cluster trip/odometer reset button (CBS reset needs no tool); BMW-capable scan tool as fallback

parts.item: Front pad set (repair kit, asbestos-free), RealOEM item for this car from 09/2009 (BMW; Bimmerworld: original pad for E9X LCI 328i from 2009; PMB lists 328i and 328i xDrive 2009-2013). RealOEM states the sensor and the brake pad paste are additional mandatory parts, so the kit does not include them.
parts.note: Correct pad kit for this VIN decode (build 09/2009, standard brakes). RealOEM front diagrams are conditioned on S100A=No / S102A=No (no usable-load increase / reinforced-brakes options), which the VIN decode shows are absent.

parts.item: Front pad set, 328i / 328i xDrive / 328xi, built after 09/2007 (predecessor number; PMB lists 2007-2010; FCP and Leebmann24 (BMW-style fitment table with production dates, E90 from 09/2007) list it)
parts.note: Predecessor kit. RealOEM for this car (09/2009) lists only 34116790759; use this number only if a parts counter confirms it by VIN. Same 312x24 brake family.

parts.item: Front pad set for cars built up to 09/2007 only (not for this car)
parts.note: Excluded: Turner and ECS both limit it to production up to 09/2007.

parts.item: Front pad set named in the Team-BHP post (listed by a retailer for 330/335-class cars, not 328i)
parts.conflicts: Do not use for a 328i unless a parts counter confirms by VIN.

parts.item: Front pad wear sensor, non-xDrive, built up to 03/2010
parts.note: RealOEM lists this sensor (up to 03/2010) in the front brake diagram for the 09/2009 build selection; the VIN decode puts this car's build at 09/2009, so this is the sensor for it. One sensor per car (driver front).

parts.item: Front pad wear sensor, non-xDrive, built from 03/2010 (Bimmerworld: supersedes 34356789440; Turner and Brembo/Febi/URO listings say 03/2010+)
parts.note: Successor number for builds from 03/2010 (Bimmerworld: supersedes 34356789440). Not the catalog number for this car's 09/2009 build selection, but a parts counter may supply it by supersession. Bowa listing gives overall length 692 mm.

parts.item: Front pad wear sensor, xDrive, built up to 03/2010
parts.note: xDrive only: not for this car (VIN decode: rear-wheel drive).

parts.item: Front pad wear sensor, xDrive, built from 03/2010 (listing description says Front Left)
parts.note: ECS lists the Bremmen version under an E84 title, so fitment text is unreliable; Turner is the only clean E90 source. xDrive only: not for this car (VIN decode: rear-wheel drive).

parts.item: Front brake rotor, ventilated 312 x 24 mm, current RealOEM number for this car (valid up to 04/2011); Bimmerworld and Turner list the predecessor numbers
parts.note: Only if the rotor is below minimum or damaged. Autodoc lists 34118848417 first among the OE numbers of Bosch 0 986 479 381 (312 mm, 23.9 mm thick). FCP also references 34116855006KIT for a 2010 328i xDrive front/rear kit (contents not stated).

parts.item: BMW low-viscosity DOT 4 brake fluid for top-off (see fluids)

parts.note: BMW brake pad paste; RealOEM lists it (quantity 2) in the front diagrams and calls it mandatory with every pad change.

parts.item: Front caliper carrier bolt: RealOEM item 'Torx screw with washer' M12x1.5x43 ZNS3 (4 per car, 2 per side). The second Turner number 34116772428 (M12x1.5x32) does not appear in this car's front or rear brake diagrams.
parts.conflicts: Part number resolved: RealOEM lists 34106864424 for the front carrier; 34116772428 is not in this car's catalog brake diagrams, so do not use it. Head-type naming still disagrees (RealOEM/Turner 'Torx', Febi 'hex bolt', how-to guides 18 mm hex); see the 18 mm socket tool row. Only needed if the carrier is removed.

parts.item: Pad wear sensor clip (clip accessory, used with the sensor up to 03/2010)
Front caliper retaining (anti-rattle) spring, 'Clip' (2 per car)
parts.note: RealOEM's pad kit notes call this the 'retaining spring': replace it on cars over 48 months old (this car is). Listed from 09/2007. Hella also advises replacing the spring on older cars.

parts.item: Front caliper guiding bolt (2 per caliper, 4 in the diagram); same number is listed for the rear caliper
parts.note: RealOEM item 'Guiding bolt'. Related: dust cap 34111163435, protective plug 34111154979, guide-bush repair kit 34216869617. Turner/ECS note 2 per caliper.

parts.item: Front rotor retaining screw, 'Inner hex bolt' M8x14 (1 per rotor)
parts.note: RealOEM item; matches the 6 mm hex rotor screw tool row.

parts.item: Wheel bolt, black, M12x1.5 (5 per wheel); RealOEM wheel diagram for style 285 (8Jx17 ET34), the style the VIN decode lists
parts.note: Only if a bolt is damaged. Wheel style 285 comes from the VIN option decode (2KU), not from a photo of the car.

fluids.item: Brake fluid, top-off only after pushing the piston back
fluids.spec: DOT 4 low-viscosity (BMW 81 22 0 142 156). Bimmerworld: low viscosity is factory fill for most 2004+ BMWs with DSC; ECS lists it first for E90 N52. Verify the cap or reservoir label before topping off.
fluids.capacity: Top-off only; no capacity needed (a full flush is about three 355 mL bottles per ECS, not part of this job).

torque.fastener: Wheel bolts (M12x1.5, 17 mm hex, 5 per wheel)
torque.conflicts: Dissent: koleso.ee wheel database lists 115 Nm (https://koleso.ee/en/valuveljed/bmw/3-series/248/e90-e91-e92-e93-2005-2010/488, no source given); FCP converts to 119 Nm / 88 lb-ft. Department 69 quotes BMW TIS (via workshop-manuals.com) for 120 Nm, but that page was not fetchable, so no primary copy was read. Searched the retrievable BMW owner's manual text (2011 E90 328i mirror): no wheel-bolt torque is stated there.

torque.fastener: Front caliper guide pins (7 mm hex socket-head)
torque.conflicts: Hexagon-head guide screw variant is listed at 35 Nm in the Bolidenforum BMW-data table. An older E36/E46 site gives 22 lb-ft (same number, different chassis, not counted). Department 69 repeats FCP, not independent.

torque.fastener: Front caliper carrier (bracket) bolts, M12x1.5, 18 mm
torque.conflicts: An unsourced forum moderator suggests about 80 Nm and warns 110 Nm can stretch the bolt; three tables (FCP, Autodoc, Bolidenforum BMW-data) and the Bimmerpost OP all say 110. A BMW data row for an aluminium caliper variant says 115 Nm (BMW 5-series page), not this car. Use 110 Nm and replace the bolts if BMW or the parts counter requires it.

torque.fastener: Rotor retaining screw (6 mm hex), only if rotor removed
Front rotor minimum (discard) thickness, 312x24 mm rotor (a limit, not a torque)
torque.conflicts: No BMW document read; these are rotor-maker catalog limits. Autodoc (Bosch 0 986 479 381, OE numbers include this car's 34118848417) 22.4, Brembo 09.B337.21 22.4 (listed for 'vehicles without sports package'), ATE 22.4 and Pelican's normally-aspirated front 22.4 all agree; febi lists 22.5, Brembo Xtra 22.6, ATE PowerDisc 21.6. The earlier 18.4 mm Pelican entry is the rear rotor value. The stamp on the rotor hat is the final authority.

torque.fastener: Wear sensor wheel-liner fasteners / junction box door
torque.value: MISSING (no spec found; do not over-tighten)
torque.conflicts: Sources only give sizes (8/10 mm). Treat as snug hand-tight plastic trim fasteners.

steps.title: Confirm parts and prepare the car
steps.instruction: Before starting, match the parts to this car (VIN decode, probable not proven: 2010 328i sedan, rear-wheel drive, built 09/2009, standard brakes, 312x24 front rotor): pad kit 34116790759, driver-front wear sensor (34356789440 plus clip 34356779356 for cars built up to 03/2010; 34356792560 for cars built from 03/2010, so check the build date on the door-jamb label or have a parts counter confirm by VIN), retaining springs 34116776526 and anti-squeal paste 83192158851 per BMW's catalog, which calls sensor and paste mandatory with every pad change. Compare the old pads and sensor with the new ones; a parts counter can confirm by VIN. Park on level ground, chock the rear wheels, put the car in Park. Open the hood and unscrew the brake-fluid reservoir cap (optional but recommended so the level can rise as the piston is pushed back); keep the cap clean. Do not press the brake pedal while any caliper is off.
warnings: Brake fluid damages paint; wipe spills at once.
Never press the brake pedal with the caliper removed.

steps.title: Loosen the wheel bolts on the ground
steps.instruction: With the car still on the ground, break each 17 mm wheel bolt loose about one turn.
warnings: If locking bolts are fitted, find the key first.

steps.title: Lift the front at the side jacking points and support it on stands
steps.instruction: Use the four side jacking points: small rectangular plastic pads at the sills, one just behind each front wheel and one ahead of each rear wheel (the BMW owner's manual shows their positions only in an illustration). Raise the front at the pad behind the wheel you are working on, place a rated jack stand under the same pad (or the pad behind the other front wheel as well), chock the opposite wheel as well as the rears, and check the car is level and stable before removing a wheel. A wood block or hockey puck between jack and pad protects the pad. Center lifting is not used in this procedure: a front center point is described in forum posts, but sources disagree about any rear center point (crossmember vs not allowed), so it is left out. Never lift on the differential.
warnings: Never work under a car held only by a jack.
Do not jack on the rear differential cover or housing.
Position of the four side pads is secondary-sourced; the BMW manual text only says 'positions shown in the illustration'.

steps.title: Remove the wheel
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts while holding the wheel, then lift it off.
warnings: Support the wheel; it is heavy.

steps.title: Remove the anti-rattle spring
steps.instruction: Pry the retaining spring off the caliper with a flat screwdriver while holding it with your other hand. Fit a new spring (34116776526): BMW's catalog says to replace it on cars over 48 months old, and Hella notes it is preloaded and fatigues. This car is far past 48 months.
warnings: The spring can fly off; wear eye protection.

steps.title: Remove the two guide pins
steps.instruction: Pop the rubber or plastic dust caps off the guide pins, clean the pin heads with a wire brush and spray lubricant, then unscrew both pins with a 7 mm hex socket until the caliper is free.
warnings: Check the hex size before turning; do not round the socket heads.
Keep the pin boots intact.

steps.title: Take the caliper off and support it
steps.instruction: Spread the pads slightly with a screwdriver or pry bar, slide the caliper off the rotor, and hang it from the spring/strut with wire or rest it on a stand.
warnings: Never let the caliper hang by the brake hose.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the wear sensor (driver side only)
steps.instruction: The front wear sensor is on the driver (left) front brake only. Pull it straight out of the inner pad, unhook its wire from the strut bracket, open the small plastic door behind the strut (or lift the cover high in the wheel well), press the connector tab and separate the plug. Skip this step on the passenger front.
warnings: Old sensors can be brittle and snap; replace the sensor with every pad change.
Passenger-side front has no sensor.

steps.title: Remove the old pads and clips
steps.instruction: Slide the outer pad out of the caliper carrier; the inner pad is held by a clip in the piston and pries out. Note the position of the metal clip that often stays on the old inner pad and any carrier abutment clips.

steps.title: Inspect and measure the rotor
steps.instruction: Check for cracks, scoring and a raised lip, and measure thickness at several points with a micrometer. New thickness is 24 mm; the catalog discard thickness is 22.4 mm and the minimum is also stamped (MIN TH) on the rotor. Replace both rotors if either is at or below the limit; if the stamp and 22.4 mm differ, replace at the larger of the two (conservative guide policy).
warnings: Replace rotors in pairs.
22.4 mm is a rotor-maker catalog limit (4 hosts agree); no BMW document was read.

steps.title: Optional branch: rotor replacement
steps.instruction: If replacing the rotor: look at the two carrier-bolt heads first (hexagon head: 18 mm socket; star-shaped head: external-Torx socket, size not found). Remove the two carrier bolts (breaker bar), lift off the carrier, remove the 6 mm rotor screw (M8x14), clean the hub face of rust, fit the new rotor and torque the screw to 16 Nm, reinstall the carrier and torque its bolts to 110 Nm, then carry on with the next step. Use the catalog carrier bolt 34106864424 if the old bolts are damaged.
warnings: Replace rotors and pads together.
Carrier bolt torque is secondary-sourced (110 Nm).
Do not force an 18 mm socket onto a star-shaped head.

steps.title: Clean and lubricate
steps.instruction: Clean the carrier abutments with a wire brush and brake cleaner (not on rubber), check the guide-pin boots, put a thin film of silicone-based caliper grease on the pin sliding surfaces only (never mineral oil near rubber), and put a thin film of anti-squeal paste on the pad backing contact points on the carrier.
warnings: Keep grease and paste off pad friction material and rotor faces.

steps.title: Retract the piston
steps.instruction: Push the piston straight back into the caliper with a wind-back tool, or with a clamp and the old inner pad put back into the caliper as a spacer (the old pads are already out), watching the reservoir so it does not overflow.
warnings: Open the reservoir cap first and mop spills.

steps.title: Fit the new pads and sensor
steps.instruction: Fit the new pads with friction material facing the rotor and the clips seated; on the driver front, press the new wear sensor (the number for your build date, see the parts list) into its channel on the inner pad with its clip, and route the wire as before. Do not reuse the old sensor; BMW's catalog lists the sensor as mandatory with the pads.
warnings: Check that the spring and clips are not bent.

steps.title: Refit the caliper and guide pins
steps.instruction: Slide the caliper over the pads and rotor, thread both guide pins in by hand, then torque them to 30 Nm. Refit the dust caps, then refit the anti-rattle spring and make sure it is seated. Reconnect the sensor plug, close the junction box door, clip the wire back.
warnings: 30 Nm is secondary-sourced only (no BMW document read).
Confirm the pin head type first (socket-head 7 mm vs hexagon-head). The catalog lists one guiding-bolt number (34111157041) for this car, used front and rear.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and torque
steps.instruction: Clean the hub contact face, optionally put a thin film of copper grease only where the rotor hat meets the wheel, mount the wheel, thread the bolts by hand, snug them, lower the car, then torque to 120 Nm in a crisscross sequence.
warnings: Torque value is secondary-sourced; BMW TIS (per Department 69) also says to re-check all wheel bolts after installation.
Do not put grease on the bolt threads or cones.

steps.title: Pump the pedal and check fluid
steps.instruction: Before starting the engine, pump the brake pedal until it is firm (about two-thirds travel). Then check the reservoir; top up to MAX with DOT 4 low-viscosity fluid and refit the cap.
warnings: Do not drive until the pedal is firm.

steps.title: Reset the brake service indicator
steps.instruction: With a new sensor fitted and ignition on (engine off), use the trip/odometer reset button to reach the brake service item, hold until RESET shows, press again to confirm. If the cluster method fails, use a BMW-capable scan tool (service functions, CBS reset, front brakes).
warnings: Reset requires the new sensor to be fitted and both axle sensors intact (Pelican staff).
Some 2010 cluster reports of failure; generic OBD tools may not reset CBS.

steps.title: Test and bed in
steps.instruction: Road-test at low speed in an empty area and check pedal feel and noise. BMW's owner's manual says the brakes need an initial break-in period of approx. 300 miles / 500 km to reach optimized contact and wear patterns, so avoid hard stops and heavy braking over that distance (Autodoc's shorter 150 to 200 km figure is superseded by BMW's). If the pad maker supplies its own bedding procedure, follow it.
warnings: Test brakes in an empty area before normal driving.

steps.title: Re-check the wheel bolts
steps.instruction: After the first short drive and again after about 50 to 100 km, re-check wheel-bolt torque.
warnings: Re-check interval is general practice; only the 'check again after installation' instruction is attributed to BMW TIS.

safety: Support the car on rated jack stands at the side jacking points on a level surface; never rely on the jack. Do not jack on the rear differential cover.
Never let the caliper hang by its brake hose and never press the pedal with the caliper off.
Brake dust may be hazardous: wet-wipe or use brake cleaner; do not blow it off with compressed air.
Do not put grease on friction surfaces; use silicone-based grease on pins and keep mineral oil off rubber boots.
Torque wheel bolts to 120 Nm crisscross and re-check after a short drive; all torques here are secondary-sourced, not from a BMW document.
Replace the wear sensor, retaining spring and use brake pad paste with every pad change (BMW catalog).
Pump the pedal to firm before moving the car, test at low speed, and treat the first 500 km (300 miles) as break-in (BMW owner's manual).
missingEvidence: No BMW torque document (TIS, Bentley) was reachable: all fastener torques are secondary. The BMW owner's manual text read does not state any torque (wheel-bolt torque not in the retrievable text).
Rotor discard thickness 22.4 mm comes from rotor-maker catalogs, not from a BMW document (febi lists 22.5).
Carrier bolt head type: RealOEM 'Torx screw with washer' vs Febi/guides 'hex 18 mm'; the external-Torx socket size was not found.
Factory torque for the wear-sensor liner fasteners (not specified anywhere found).
Which hex size is used on this exact car's guide pins is only 6-vs-7 mm unresolved in one staff reply; 7 mm is the majority.
Exact placement of the two guide pins (top/bottom or front/back) and the exact shape of the retaining spring are not established (visual gaps).

Positions of the four side jacking pads are described only by forum posts; the BMW manual text refers to an illustration that could not be read. Whether a front or rear center lift point is approved by BMW is unresolved (forums disagree).
Wheel-bolt re-check interval after installation is general practice; BMW's instruction is only attributed via Department 69.
FCP's front and rear video walkthroughs are not transcribed (video only).

visuals.title: Front caliper: spring, dust caps, guide pins and carrier bolts

elements.describe: A floating disc-brake caliper straddling the rotor, seen from the outboard side with the wheel removed.
A spring retaining clip fitted on the caliper, pried out with a flat screwdriver.
Rubber or plastic caps covering the ends of the guide pins.
Two guide pins with hex-socket heads that hold the caliper to the carrier; they unthread to free the caliper.
Two larger hex-head bolts behind the caliper that hold the carrier bracket to the steering knuckle.

facts.note: 3 sites say it is a spring on the caliper that is pried off; exact routing/shape is not established.
3 sites: hex socket (7 mm per FCP/Autodoc; 6 mm per one Pelican staff reply).
Gap: no source says where the two guide pins sit (top/bottom or front/back).
4 sites: 18 mm hex head, two bolts.
3 sites: two bolts from behind, carrier secured to the steering knuckle.

Sources describe the caliper sitting on the rotor with the bracket behind it and being tied up off the brake hose; none gives a richer placement statement, so only the generic straddling-rotor placement is supported.
All four describe an anti-rattle spring/clip on the caliper pried out with a flat screwdriver.
Autodoc: dust-boot caps of the guide pins; Team-BHP: two plastic caps hiding the caliper bolts; Pelican: rubber plugs on the caliper mounting fasteners.
FCP: 7mm hex caliper guide pins (separate from 18mm bolts); Autodoc: hex bit fastening plus guide pins; Team-BHP and Pelican: hex/Allen caliper bolts. Size varies by source (6, 7, 17mm cited).
Team-BHP: one top, one bottom under caps; Autodoc and FCP: guide pins hold the caliper to its bracket.

mustNotDepict.reason: Exact bend shape, orientation and routing are not established.
Top/bottom or front/back placement of the two pins is not established.
Brand (ATE/Teves), colour and size depend on brake package and are not established for this car.

https://club.autodoc.co.uk/manuals/how-t.establishes: Spring, dust caps, guide pins with H7 hex bit, caliper removal order, 30 Nm and 120 Nm.

https://www.fcpeuro.com/blog/how-to-repl.establishes: Guide pins 7 mm hex 30 Nm; carrier bolts 18 mm 110 Nm; wheel nuts 119 Nm (E90 incl. 328i).

https://www.pelicanparts.com/BMW/techart.establishes: Spring, rubber plugs, sensor on driver front, plastic door behind strut.

https://www.hella.com/hella-tech-world-a.establishes: Teves FN caliper steps, retaining spring, guide screws, wear indicator replacement.

https://club.autodoc.se/pdf-manuals/club.establishes: Carrier bolts socket 18 at 110 Nm, guide pins H7 at 30 Nm, rotor screw H6 at 16 Nm.

https://drivediy.dozuki.com/Guide/BMW+3+.establishes: Two caliper (carrier) bolts 18 mm front, one top and one bottom; sensor driver front.

https://www.pelicanparts.com/BMW/techart.establishes: Two bracket bolts 18 mm front; 6 mm rotor fastener.

https://www.turnermotorsport.com/BMW-E90.establishes: Front carrier is secured to the steering knuckle.

gapFillNotes: Carrier bolt head: RealOEM names part 34106864424 'Torx screw with washer' (M12x1.5x43) while four how-to sources say 18 mm hex head; the visual should not show a head shape until this is resolved.

visuals.title: Front pad wear sensor and its connector (driver side only)

elements.describe: A thin wear-sensor wire clipped into the inner brake pad, running up out of the caliper area.
A small plastic junction box with a door, high in the wheel well behind the strut, holding the sensor plug with a release tab.
A bracket on the strut that the sensor wire is hooked to.

facts.note: 3 sites: driver (left) front brake only; sensor is on the inner pad (inner per Autodoc/youcanic rear article).
2 sites: plastic door/black box high in the wheel well behind the strut.
2 sites say a connector release tab is pressed; actual tab shape is not described.
1 site only (wire unhooked from the strut bracket).
Pelican, YouCanic, DriveDIY and Team-BHP all describe a wear sensor wire in the front pad on the driver side only.
Pelican: plastic door behind the front strut; YouCanic and BMWTuning: black box on the wheel well with the connector; Bimmerpost: front plug in junction box behind the strut.

mustNotDepict.reason: Exact box shape, door hinge and plug design are not established.
Passenger-side front has no sensor; depict only the driver side.

https://www.pelicanparts.com/BMW/techart.establishes: Front sensor on driver-side pad; plastic door behind strut; connector tab.

https://www.youcanic.com/bmw-brake-pad-w.establishes: Front-left sensor, black box on wheel well, release tab, wire on strut bracket.
